prompt: To cleanly convert 1-butyne to cis-1-butene (Z-alkene), which reagent set works?

options.label: H₂ with Lindlar's catalyst (Pd/CaCO₃ poisoned with quinoline)
Na in liquid NH₃ at −33 °C (dissolving metal reduction)
H₂ with Pd/C at atmospheric pressure
LiAlH₄ in dry ether, then aqueous workup

explanation: Lindlar (poisoned Pd) stops cleanly at the Z-alkene (syn-addition of H₂ with no over-reduction). Na/NH₃(l) gives the E-alkene (anti-addition via radical anion). H₂/Pd goes all the way to the alkane. LiAlH₄ doesn't reduce alkynes.
